title: A counter program count-down loop
statement: Let $P$ be a counter program on a binary input $x$, with labels $h,d,c,z$ and register $r$. Suppose the instruction at $h$ tests $r$, going to $z$ if it is zero and to $d$ otherwise, and the instruction at $d$ decrements $r$ and goes to $c$. Let $K,b\in\mathbb{N}$, and for each $j\in\mathbb{N}$ let $\sigma_j$ be a register assignment, $p_j$ an input position, and $e_j$ an output string. Assume $\sigma_j(r)=K-j$ for every $j\le K$, and that for every $j<K$, from label $c$ with register assignment obtained from $\sigma_j$ by setting register $r$ to $K-j-1$ and input position $p_j$, the program reaches label $h$ with registers $\sigma_{j+1}$ and input position $p_{j+1}$ within at most $b$ steps, appending $e_j$ to every initial output string. Then from label $h$ with registers $\sigma_0$ and input position $p_0$, the program reaches label $z$ with registers $\sigma_K$ and input position $p_K$ within at most $K(b+2)+1$ steps, appending the concatenation of $e_0,e_1,\ldots,e_{K-1}$ to every initial output string.
hypotheses_covered: The instruction at $h$ is a zero test on $r$, with zero destination $z$ and nonzero destination $d$
The instruction at $d$ decrements $r$ and goes to $c$
For every $j<K$, the stated run from the modified $\sigma_j$ at $c$ reaches $h$ with $\sigma_{j+1}$ and $p_{j+1}$ within $b$ steps, appending $e_j$
replaced:
Let $P$ be a counter program on a binary input $x$, $r$ a register, and
$h, d, c, z$ labels such that the instruction at $h$ is
$\mathsf{jz}(r, z, d)$ (go to $z$ if register $r$ is zero, else to $d$) and the
instruction at $d$ is $\mathsf{dec}(r, c)$.  Let $K, b \in \mathbb{N}$, and for
each $j \in \mathbb{N}$ let $\sigma_j$ be a register vector, $p_j$ an input
position and $e_j$ a bit string, with $\sigma_j(r) = K - j$ for all $j \le K$.
Suppose that for every $j < K$, from label $c$ with registers $\sigma_j$ modified
so that register $r$ holds $K - j - 1$, and $p_j$ symbols read, $P$ reaches label
$h$ with registers $\sigma_{j+1}$ and $p_{j+1}$ symbols read within $b$ steps
while appending $e_j$ to its output.  Then from label $h$ with registers
$\sigma_0$ and $p_0$ symbols read, $P$ reaches label $z$ with registers
$\sigma_K$ and $p_K$ symbols read within $K(b+2)+1$ steps while appending the
concatenation $e_0 e_1 \cdots e_{K-1}$.
